_about: Tracked WER baseline for whisperquiet dictation. The point is to make the accuracy gap explicit and queryable instead of buried in commit messages. Update via: scripts/bench_wer.py scripts/bench-sentences.txt --takes N --json results/baseline.json (records the best variant of a run). WER here is NORMALIZED (lowercased, punctuation stripped, whitespace-split) per scripts/bench_wer.py:wer, scored against the full concatenation of the reference lines.
design_note: DESIGN.md success bar is >=95% word accuracy (<=5% WER) on whispered speech in a quiet room. The 'real recordings' measurement below is ~11 points short of that — closing this gap is the Phase 0 goal.

measurements.note: Best variant of the WER grid; staccato vocab prompt beat the plain glossary (18.9 -> 16.3). Per-take counts not retained — recorded from the commit narrative, not a results file. Treat as historical, not reproducible.

pending: Fresh REPRODUCIBLE quiet-room baseline: record 2-3 full reads of scripts/bench-sentences.txt in a quiet room, then run scripts/bench_wer.py ... --json results/baseline.json so the number is regenerable, not narrated.
Noisy/cafe baseline: same reads with cafe/fan/AC background, to quantify the noise gap and feed scripts/bench_denoise.py.
Whispered baseline: same reads spoken at dictation volume (whisper), the actual core use case and the worst-WER condition.
